correctness.rationale: With exactly specified \(t\ge2\) and \(\ell\ge2\), the Gram vectors have positive inner product exactly on ordinary cube edges, span \(\ell-1\) dimensions and give \(M\ge t+2\). Explicit color-change sequences construct \(t+2\) forcing sets. At that size the brush true-twin obstruction allows \(t\) or \(t-1\) initially black brush vertices; the first-move white-neighbor classification is exhaustive and gives exactly \(3+4t\) minimizers for \(\ell\ge3\). For \(\ell=2\), the cube is \(K_{t+3}\). Exact finite checks corroborate 32 cases but are not the proof.

Primary papers on minimum rank of powers of trees address paths, strict powers and tree squares. value.rationale: The two-parameter asymmetric spider family is a natural complement to the equal-arm cases investigated in recent graph-power zero forcing. For unbounded handle length, the optimum minimizer count is the non-obvious, length-independent \(4t+3\), with an exact structural description and sharp rank witness. This goes beyond checking a small graph or restating a minimum-size bound and can serve as an exact testbed for graph-power and twin-expansion enumerators.
